# Vocabulary and branding audit

Report only. No code, schema, config, or content was changed to produce this file.

Repo: aimed-jobseek, a fork of Aimed Outreach being converted into a job-seeker product. Internal identifiers stay so the fork can cherry-pick upstream. User-facing copy and model prompts are the change surface.

## Method

Every text file in the repo was scanned except `node_modules`, `.git`, `.next`, `dist`, and `coverage`. Matches use word boundaries, including camelCase, snake_case, and kebab-case parts (`productId` matches product; `production` and `personalization` do not). Plurals are included. Phrase terms (`ideal customer`, `value proposition`, `sales rep`, `buying signal`, and the rest of the phrase list) consume their words so they are not also counted as the shorter word. Template-literal interpolations (`${product.name}`) are identifiers, not copy. Code comments are class F because TypeScript, SQL, and Prisma comments are not rendered.

Classification is one label per hit. A string that is clearly an import path, `use client`, package metadata, or an API client is F. If a string could not be traced to a screen, a model call, or an email, it is H.

## 2. Hits by classification

### A. USER-FACING COPY

Text a job seeker, or a platform operator using the admin console, can see. Includes nav labels, form copy, placeholders, empty states, errors returned to the client, onboarding, and legal pages. Recommended action is **rewrite copy** from the future vocabulary module, not an in-place synonym swap. Route paths are in H so labels can change while URLs stay mergeable.

Rows: **1080**.

The baseline templates in `src/lib/transactional-email/templates.ts` (verification, welcome, password reset, password changed, invitation, invitation accepted, cadence digest, usage limit, support ticket) do not contain the searched nouns prospect, persona, ICP, product, or campaign. ## 3. LLM prompt inventory

Every distinct prompt found. "Structural sales framing" means the prompt's job, examples, or schema assume a seller pitching a product to a buyer. Those need a rewrite of the task, not a glossary swap. Field names inside the JSON (`product`, `persona`, `painPoints`) are internal and can stay; the instructions around them cannot.

| Prompt | File | Pipeline | Structural sales framing |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Outbound email system prompt, version 18 | `src/lib/email-generation/prompt.ts` (`SYSTEM_PROMPT`) | email generation | **Yes.** Writes one-to-one outbound email. Priority order is offer, call to action, pain-led opening, then product. Persona is "which value prop leads" and which objections to preempt. Requires an actionable close in every cold outbound email. Forbids "I can walk through it" unless it asks the reader to act. Examples of acceptable closes include "Would you be open to a 20-minute review?", "Book a free estimate today.", and "Reply with the best person to speak with." Invalid example is a demo offer. Opening approaches include "selling motion", "decision or approval moment", and "role-specific tradeoff". Audience payload includes `personaBuyingRole` and `personaDecisionInfluence`. |
| Email user payload | `src/lib/email-generation/prompt.ts` (`buildEmailPrompt`) | email generation | **Yes.** User message is "Generate the first outbound email for this campaign contact." Payload carries offer, CTA, pain points, product claims, proof points, objections, and ICP definition. |
| Length and structure instructions | same file, `emailStructure` | email generation | **Yes.** Fixed shape is problem paragraph, then how the product solves it, then offer and action. |
| Follow-up guidance | `followUpGuidance` in the same file, appended by `src/lib/email-generation/prepare-email-generation.ts` | email generation | **Yes.** Later sequence steps must rotate product feature, positioning theme, proof point, or offer. Explicitly says not to paraphrase the same problem → solution → ask sequence. "the rep's selected length" treats the user as a sales rep. |
| Reply strategy | `replyStrategy` in `prompt.ts`, used by `buildReplyEmailPrompt` | reply drafting | **Yes.** INTERESTED reinforces value and proposes a next step. OBJECTION answers with evidence. NOT_NOW says "avoid continuing the pitch". NOT_INTERESTED says "stop selling" and do not manufacture another pitch. |
| Reply draft wrapper | `src/lib/email-generation/prepare-email-generation.ts` (`buildReplyEmailPrompt`) | reply drafting | **Yes.** "Draft a direct reply to the prospect" and "Do not restart the original outbound pitch." |
| Personalization tiers | `src/lib/email-generation/personalization.ts` (`PERSONALIZATION_TIER_INSTRUCTIONS`) | email generation | **Yes.** BEST and COMPANY tiers tell the model to infer selling motion and connect it to the problem this product solves. THIN tier is a "persona-and-product email". UI labels in the same file ("Company selling motion", "Persona and product only") are user-facing and also sales-framed. |
| Company-research use | `src/lib/email-generation/company-research-use.ts` | email generation, fact selection | **Yes.** Instructs the model to infer deal complexity, cycle length, stakeholder count, buying centers, and customer type, then connect that motion to the product. |
| Required motion specifics | `src/lib/email-generation/motion-specifics.ts` (`REQUIRED_MOTION_SPECIFICS_INSTRUCTIONS`) | fact selection, email generation | **Yes.** Facts are chosen because they suggest this persona has the problem this product solves. |
| Fact selector | `src/lib/email-generation/semantic-fact-selector.ts` (`buildFactSelectionMessages`) | fact selection | **Yes.** "You select company-research facts for outbound email personalization." Selection test is "THIS persona has THIS problem that THIS product solves" and "this prospect plausibly has that problem". |
| Claim guard | `src/lib/email-generation/claim-validation.ts` | claim guard | **Yes, as a sales claim checker.** The rep is trusted; the model must not invent product capabilities, offer terms, or facts about the prospect. The guard is useful for a job seeker (do not invent the candidate), but it is written as product-claim and prospect-claim enforcement. Rewrite the protected object (candidate facts, not product claims) or the guard will keep treating the candidate as a product. |
| Regeneration retry | `src/lib/email-generation/service.ts` (system addendum around the failed draft) | email generation | **Yes.** Rewrite instruction still says reason from a company specific to the executive problem and do not open with product capabilities. |
| Prospect reply classifier | `src/lib/email-generation/reply.ts` (`classifyProspectReply`) | reply drafting | **Yes.** Categories are INTERESTED, OBJECTION, REFERRAL, NOT_NOW, NOT_INTERESTED for a prospect reply. Referral means they direct the sender to another person. That taxonomy is a sales inbox, not a hiring-manager reply. |
| Offer validation | `src/lib/campaign/offer-validation.ts` (`validateOfferSemantically`) | other (campaign offer) | **Yes.** Validates an offer against product restrictions, avoided terminology, and product evidence. The feature assumes a campaign offer. |
| Product setup synthesis | `src/lib/product-research/prompt.ts` (`buildProductSynthesisMessages`) | research (candidate profile, today "product") | **Yes.** "Production Product setup synthesis engine." Output includes value proposition, problems solved, buyer functions, customer evidence, and `suggestedBuyerRoles` (buyer / user / influencer). Example roles are "Chief Revenue Officer" and "Revenue Operations Leader". It forbids campaigns and email generation in this step, but the profile it builds is a thing being sold. |
| Persona synthesis | `src/lib/persona-research/prompt.ts` (`buildPersonaSynthesisMessages`) | research (target role, today "persona") | **Yes.** "Expert GTM Persona research analyst." Persona is defined as a buyer role. "Desired Outcomes From Solution" are outcomes from using the customer's product, explicitly not meeting or demo goals. Negative signals are people who are not the buyer, with an example "Sales representative focused primarily on individual quota". Differentiation is what they are measured on and what lands on their desk. This is a buying-committee model. |
| Persona interpretation | `src/lib/interpretation/persona-prompt.ts` | other (criteria from a persona form) | **Yes.** "Production buyer-persona interpretation engine." Pain points "make a solution relevant." Desired outcomes are what the buyer wants from adopting a solution. It spends several rules separating those outcomes from campaign CTAs, meetings, and demos, which shows the data model was built next to a sales motion. |
| ICP interpretation | `src/lib/interpretation/icp.ts` (`buildIcpInterpretationMessages`) | other (criteria from an ICP form) | **Yes.** "Production ICP interpretation engine." Primary tier is "firmographics that define the customer". Worked example: "Sells complex multi-stakeholder deals" is a semantic criterion. The task is "which companies should we sell to." |
| Company research | `src/lib/research/prompt.ts` (`buildCompanyResearchMessages`) | research | **Yes.** Asks what they sell, who they sell to, business model, public buying/growth signals, and AOV or deal size. Schema fields include `whatTheySell`, `customerTypes`, `buyingSignals`, `estimatedAov`. Fit against product, ICP, and persona is deferred to scoring, but the research itself is commercial-intelligence shaped. A job seeker still needs employer research; the questions have to change from "what they buy" to "how they hire." |
| Product source discovery | `src/lib/research/web-search-retriever.ts` | research | **Partial.** Finds official pages, docs, pricing, case studies, and reviews for a named product or company. Pricing and case studies are sales-site assumptions. Rewrite the source types for a candidate profile (résumé, portfolio, public work) versus an employer site. |
| Contact role research | `src/lib/contact-research/service.ts` (`buildContactResearchMessages`) | research | **Partial.** "What a contact is responsible for" from public evidence, judged against persona criteria. The task (what does this person own) can survive. The criteria it is pointed at are buyer-role criteria from the persona prompt. Rewrite together with persona interpretation. |
| Prospect scoring | `src/lib/scoring/prompt.ts` (`buildScoringMessages`) | other (scoring) | **Yes.** "Evidence-based B2B prospect scoring analyst." Scores "HOW STRONG a prospect THIS contact at THIS company is for THIS Product against THIS ICP and THIS Persona." Allows disqualifiers from ICP negatives and persona exclusions. Says "No sales fluff" while doing sales qualification. |
| Title suggestion | `src/lib/scoring/title-suggestion-prompt.ts` | other (scoring) | **Yes.** Maps unmatched job titles onto buyer personas for a B2B product. Examples are "VP of Sales Operations", "President of Sales", and a generic CEO who may not be a buyer. |

UI copy that is shown as "Prompt examples" and then stored as campaign guidance (so it can enter the email prompt) lives in `src/components/EmailGuidancePromptExamples.tsx`. The examples are sales-email instructions ("ask for a reply instead of a meeting", "leave out pricing"). They are class A because the job seeker sees them, and they also become model input. Rewrite them with the email prompt.

No separate voice-matching system prompt exists. Voice is the first writing sample pasted into the email prompt ("match its sentence length... closing style") in `SYSTEM_PROMPT`. There is no few-shot library of sales emails in production code. The sales emails in tests and persona fixtures are fixtures, not few-shot prompts.

JSON schemas sent to the model are inline in the prompt files above (`responseSchema` blocks), not a second hidden prompt file. `src/lib/ai/structured-output-schemas.ts` names operations (`emailClaimValidation`, `prospectReplyClassification`, `campaignOfferValidation`, `productSourceDiscovery`) and is an internal identifier surface (class F) unless a description string there is also sent; the descriptions inspected are in the prompt files already listed.

## 5. Features that may not map to job seeking

Decisions only. Nothing here is a recommendation to remove a feature.

| Feature | What it does today | Decision needed |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Campaigns | A named outbound effort with setup, list, companies, contacts, emails, and report stages (`src/lib/workflow/campaign-stages.ts`). Nav label "Campaigns". | Whether a job search keeps a "campaign" object (one search, one target role) or the word and the stage model both change. Identifiers can stay either way. |
| Sequences and cadence | Multi-step follow-up, daily digest of contacts due, stop-sequence. Digest subject is "{{dueCount}} follow-up(s) due". | Whether a job seeker runs a timed follow-up sequence with a morning digest, or a simpler reminder. |
| Offers and CTAs | Campaign offer name, description, CTA, and notes are required email context and have their own validator. | What the "ask" is when you are not selling. A reply, a conversation, or an application are different prompts. |
| Meeting and demo asks | Prompt examples treat a meeting or demo as the default close ("book a free estimate", "20-minute review", "instead of a meeting"). | Whether the product should ever ask a hiring manager for a meeting, and which asks are forbidden. |
| ICP | Company firmographics and "who should buy", with primary criteria that define the customer and secondary signals that never disqualify. | Target employers (size, industry, geography) fit the mapping. Buying-motion criteria ("sells complex deals", tech-stack, competitor replacement) may not. |
| Personas as buyer roles | Title, seniority, pain, desired outcomes from "your solution", objections, buying role, decision influence, and exclusions for non-buyers. | Target role fits the mapping. Buyer, champion, quota-carrying rep, and economic buyer do not, unless the job seeker is explicitly modeling a hiring committee. |
| Prospect scoring | Scores a contact at a company as a prospect for a product. Buckets are shown as "Ready to include", "Check before including", and "Left out". | Whether fit scoring remains, and what "fit" means (role match and employer match, not buying intent). |
| Company research | What the company sells, who it sells to, AOV, buying signals, risk signals. | Employer research for a job seeker needs hiring, team, and product facts. Buying-signal and deal-size research may be the wrong job. |
| Contact research | Public evidence of what a person owns, scored against persona criteria. | Can map to "what this recruiter or hiring manager owns" if the criteria stop being buyer criteria. |
| Claim guard and supported claims | Stops the model inventing product capabilities and prospect facts. | Keep a guard. The protected facts become the candidate's real history, not a product's proof points. |
| Voice | One writing sample controls cadence and closing style of the sales email. | Keep voice matching. The instructions about closing style assume a sales close. |
| Reply classes | Interested, objection, referral, not now, not interested. | A hiring manager's reply is not a sales objection. The classes need a product decision before the prompt is rewritten. |
| Seats and shared campaigns | Team plan is 2–10 seats, shared campaigns, per-seat company allowances. Enterprise seat cap is "set by Sales Forecaster". | Whether job seekers have teams and shared searches, or the product is single-player. The seat schema can stay while the copy waits. |
| Referrals | Share message sells Aimed Outreach as a prospect-research and outbound-email tool, with a lasting percent-off coupon. | The coupon mechanic can stay. The share sentence cannot. |
| Lists, contacts, mailbox send | Lists of people, Microsoft mailbox sending, suppression. | Closest to the job-seeker product (people to write to, sent from the user's own mailbox). The nouns "contact" and "list" still need vocabulary, which is why they are called out even though bare "contact" was not a search term. |
| Qualification exclusions | Persona negative signals drop people who are not the buyer (quota-carrying reps, CRM admins). | Excluding the wrong audience may remain. The reasons must stop being sales-role reasons. |
| Sample product in fixtures | `src/lib/persona-research/fixtures/` describes a sales-forecasting product (deals, quota, pipeline, reps). | This is example tenant data about a product that itself is a sales tool. Replacing it is a test-data decision, separate from renaming the app. |

Additional sales-domain language found outside the required term list, concentrated in prompts and UI rather than dumped as every identifier:

- GTM (persona research prompt)
- CTA, call to action, offer
- pitch, selling, selling motion, stop selling
- objection, proof point, positioning
- buyer role, buying center, buying role, decision influence
- disqualifier / disqualify
- cadence, follow-up
- seat
- AOV, what they sell, who they sell to
- "VP Sales" in the contact-import placeholder
- Nav and stage label "Contacts" (the mapping says contact → recruiter or hiring manager)

Bare `contact` identifiers were not row-listed. They are the upstream schema name and should stay. The user-visible label "Contacts" should be treated as class A when the vocabulary module lands.

## 6. Proposed vocabulary module

Proposal only. Not implemented.

**One module, consumed everywhere copy is assembled.** Add something like `src/lib/vocabulary/jobseek.ts` that exports a frozen object: product name, short name, support email, enterprise contact, app URL usage note, and the user-facing nouns and verbs (`candidate`, `target role`, `target employers`, `hiring manager`, and the sentence-level labels for nav, stages, empty states, and billing). Frontend components, server actions, email templates, and prompt builders import that object. They do not keep their own string literals for those nouns.

**Prompts reference it by slot, not by search-and-replace.** Each prompt builder interpolates vocabulary into a job-seeker task statement ("write to a hiring manager about this candidate"), then passes the existing JSON keys (`product`, `persona`, `icp`, `campaign`) unchanged so upstream code still merges. The schema keys stay sales-shaped. The instructions, examples, and forbidden moves are rewritten for the job-seeker task and may quote the vocabulary object's labels when they mention what the user sees. A prompt test should fail if the system string still contains a fixed denylist (`outbound`, `prospect`, `value prop`, `pitch`, `selling motion`, `demo`) unless the line is explicitly marked as an internal key name.

**Mergeability.** Do not rename Prisma models, columns, enums, function names, or route paths. Upstream bugfixes that touch `product` or `campaign` still apply. The vocabulary module is fork-only; keep it in a directory upstream does not have, and keep prompt edits isolated to the template strings so a cherry-pick conflict is a string conflict, not a rename conflict. Where upstream and the fork must diverge in a prompt's meaning, comment the fork-only block with the upstream prompt version constant that already exists (`EMAIL_GENERATION_PROMPT_VERSION` and the other `*_PROMPT_VERSION` constants) so a version bump upstream is visible.

**Files that change when it is adopted:** every file with an A, B, C, D, E, or G hit, plus the new module. Count from this audit: **305**. H rows are extra files that may join that set after the decisions in section 5. F files are not part of the adoption set.

Class file counts used for that estimate: A 125, B 20, C 1, D 14, E 19, G 133. H files that still need a decision: 193. F files left untouched: 579.
